title: SAP HANA
description: SAP HANA — SAP HANA Cloud, an on-premise HANA (the database under S/4HANA and BW/4HANA), or HANA express.

fields.name: host
fields.label: Host
fields.help: Paste the SQL endpoint as HANA shows it — with or without :port.

fields.name: port
fields.label: Port
fields.help: HANA Cloud: 443. On-premise: 3<instance>15 for a single database, 3<instance>41 or the tenant's own for a tenant.

fields.name: database
fields.label: Tenant database
fields.help: Only for an on-premise system with tenant databases reached through the system database's port. Leave it empty for HANA Cloud.

fields.name: tls
fields.label: Encrypted connection
fields.help: HANA Cloud always encrypts. Turn it off only for a database on your own network that has no certificate.

fields.name: schemas
fields.label: Schemas
fields.help: Leave empty for every schema the user may read.

setup.title: Where the database is
setup.say:
The SQL endpoint of your HANA database, as the engine reaches it. In SAP HANA Cloud Central: your instance → Actions → Copy SQL Endpoint, and paste it here (the port comes with it).

For an on-premise HANA, the host and its SQL port. If the database lets in only known addresses (HANA Cloud's allowed connections, a firewall), let the engine's machine in first.

fix.say: Nothing answers at {host}. Check the endpoint and port — and, for HANA Cloud, that the instance is running and its allowed connections include the engine's address.

setup.title: A user that may read
setup.say: Superatom only reads. Give it a user of its own that may read and nothing more — run this as an administrator (in the SQL console of SAP HANA Cloud Central or the Database Explorer), choosing a password and naming your schema:

copy.label: Make a read-only user

fix.say: HANA refused {user}'s password. Check it — and that the user is not locked or waiting for a first password change (create it with NO FORCE_FIRST_PASSWORD_CHANGE).
The encrypted connection could not be made. HANA Cloud needs it on; for an on-premise database without a certificate, turn Encrypted connection off.

setup.title: Which schemas
setup.say: Leave it empty to read every schema the user may read, or name the ones to read (SALES, FINANCE). The check counts the tables and views it may read there.

fix.say: Signed in, but {user} may read no table there. Grant it SELECT on the schema (the commands in the step before), or name a schema it may read.
